title: Loop 005 Causal Route Atlas v001
question: At the current resolution of direct human causal evidence, does felt affect depend on one globally necessary/sufficient anatomical route, or do the data favor multiple substitutable/distributed causal routes?
scope: Human causal lesion, pharmacological deafferentation/blockade, and direct intracranial stimulation evidence with subjective affect whenever available.

definitions.global_necessity: A candidate route is globally necessary only if removing it abolishes the target class of felt affect across relevant elicitation routes. A verified counterexample with the target feeling preserved refutes the universal claim, while route/content-specific necessity may remain.
definitions.isolated_sufficiency: A candidate route counts as isolatedly sufficient only if its selective activation reliably evokes the target felt affect and evidence excludes the interpretation that stimulation merely recruits a wider necessary network.
definitions.modulation: A perturbation changes intensity/probability/quality of feeling without demonstrating necessity or sufficiency.
definitions.route_substitution: A target feeling remains possible through a causally distinct elicitation route after loss/attenuation of a canonical route.
definitions.route_multiplicity: Direct perturbations at multiple anatomically distinct sites can evoke overlapping reported affective states.
definitions.degeneracy_warning: Multiple effective sites do not by themselves prove independent sufficient generators; they may converge on a shared downstream network. Therefore the atlas uses EVIDENCE_FAVORS_ROUTE_MULTIPLICITY, not a claim of proven independent generators.

rules.necessity_kill: A high-confidence direct human lesion/loss result preserving the relevant feeling sets global_necessity=false for that exact candidate, but does not erase content-specific roles.
rules.stimulation_caution: Direct stimulation that evokes a feeling supports causal participation. It does not establish isolated sufficiency when spread/network propagation is plausible.
rules.physiology_dissociation: Reliable autonomic physiology without subjective emotion counts against equations of that stimulated route's autonomic output with felt presence.
rules.no_behavior_proxy: Social cognition, recognition, choice, or autonomic output alone are not treated as direct evidence of current subjective feeling.
rules.null_preservation: Null and negative findings are retained.

evidence.result: 35% CO2 evoked fear and panic attacks in all three lesion patients
evidence.source: Feinstein et al. 2013, Nature Neuroscience, DOI 10.1038/nn.3323, PMID 23377128
evidence.inference: Refutes universal amygdala necessity for human fear/panic; does not refute amygdala importance for exteroceptive/anticipatory fear.

evidence.perturbation: bilateral amygdala damage plus peripheral beta-adrenergic agonist
evidence.result: isoproterenol induced anxiety in both patients and full panic in one
evidence.source: Khalsa et al. 2016, Frontiers in Human Neuroscience, PMCID PMC4804013
evidence.inference: Supports amygdala-independent cardiorespiratory/interoceptive routes to aversive feeling.

evidence.target: autonomic defensive state and subjective emotion
evidence.result: 9 patients: dose-dependent EDA increase and HR deceleration were reliable; subjective emotional responses occurred only in a minority (2/9)
evidence.source: Inman et al. 2018/2020, Human Brain Mapping, PMID 29551365, PMCID PMC6139084
evidence.inference: Amygdala activation can drive defensive autonomic physiology without felt emotion; simple autonomic-output=feeling sufficiency is unsupported.

evidence.perturbation: complete bilateral insular destruction in patient B after herpes encephalitis
evidence.result: pain, pleasure, hunger, thirst, happiness, sadness, apprehension, irritation, caring and compassion remained reportable
evidence.source: Damasio et al. 2013, Cerebral Cortex, DOI 10.1093/cercor/bhs077, PMID 22473895
evidence.inference: Refutes the insula as a universally necessary exclusive platform for feeling; single-case and extensive additional lesions limit population generalization.

evidence.result: insula stimulation can evoke visceral/autonomic sensations; anxiety/foreboding occurred at a small subset of anterior/middle insular contacts
evidence.source: Subjective states induced by intracranial electrical stimulation matches the cytoarchitectonic organization of the human insula, PMCID PMC10893903
evidence.inference: Insula can causally contribute to conscious bodily/affective states but responses are heterogeneous and do not establish isolated/global sufficiency.

evidence.perturbation: 12,088 direct bipolar stimulations in 203 epilepsy patients
evidence.result: 115 emotional sensations; fear/anxiety associated with amygdala, anterior cingulate, hippocampus, anterior insula and frontal operculum; about half of emotional sensations occurred without a reported visceral sensation
evidence.source: Visceral and emotional responses to direct electrical stimulations of the cortex, 2023, PMCID PMC9852394
evidence.inference: Overlapping affective experiences can be evoked from multiple distinct limbic/operculo-insular sites.

evidence.perturbation: direct electrical stimulation case series plus literature review
evidence.result: emotions were evoked from superior frontal gyrus, frontal/parietal operculum, insula, middle cingulate, amygdala, hippocampus
evidence.source: Emotional experience elicited by direct electrical stimulation: Case series and literature review, 2023, PMCID PMC10235553
evidence.inference: Reinforces anatomical route multiplicity; stimulation spread prevents isolated-node sufficiency claims.

evidence.perturbation: direct electrical stimulation in one intracranially monitored patient
evidence.result: reproducible profound shame, sadness and fear; single pulses also evoked responses in amygdala, hippocampus, vmPFC/OFC, ACC and insula
evidence.source: Parvizi et al. 2022, Brain Stimulation, DOI 10.1016/j.brs.2022.04.008, PMID 35413481
evidence.inference: Supports hypothalamic causal importance but simultaneously demonstrates rapid network recruitment; isolated hypothalamic sufficiency is not established.

evidence.perturbation: neurosurgical stimulation summarized in human panic literature
evidence.result: dPAG stimulation in humans reported to induce autonomic arousal and subjective anxiety
evidence.source: Graeff et al. 1995, Psychiatry Research, DOI 10.1016/0165-1781(95)02673-k, PMID 7480384
evidence.inference: Supports a brainstem route capable of contributing to panic-like feeling; global necessity remains untested.

evidence.perturbation: peripheral autonomic denervation in pure autonomic failure
evidence.result: patients were broadly unimpaired on motivational decision-making, emotion recognition, theory of mind and social cognition; emotional attribution showed a mild deficit
evidence.inference: Strongly weakens claims that ongoing peripheral autonomic feedback is globally necessary for emotional/social functioning, but does not by itself establish preservation of every current feeling.

evidence.perturbation: randomized double-blind crossover atenolol/metoprolol/placebo before 35% CO2
evidence.result: beta blockers lowered tonic heart rate and blood pressure, but fear, discomfort and panic symptom responses did not differ by drug condition
evidence.source: de Vos et al. 2024, Psychopharmacology, DOI 10.1007/s00213-024-06548-2, PMID 38363344
evidence.inference: Beta1 adrenergic tone is not a demonstrated necessary carrier of CO2-induced subjective panic; relative HR response and other body channels remained.

evidence.perturbation: false faster versus slower cardiac feedback in public pain dataset
evidence.result: project reanalysis found robust subjective feedback effects not detectably mediated by HR, HRd or HRd_Z
evidence.source: Parrotta et al. 2026 eLife DOI 10.7554/eLife.90013; project runs 37202673284 and 37202996664
evidence.inference: Constrains strict measured-cardiac mediation only; does not establish body independence or a phenomenal bearer.

atlas_gate.route_multiplicity_requires: At least one large human DES dataset with subjective emotion from >=3 anatomically distinct regions.
atlas_gate.substitution_requires: At least one verified loss of a canonical candidate with preservation of the same affect class through another elicitation route.
atlas_gate.physiology_feeling_dissociation_requires: A direct perturbation that reliably changes emotion-related physiology while subjective emotion is absent in most tested cases.
atlas_gate.single_anatomical_source_survives_only_i: No candidate necessity counterexample exists and a selective sufficiency/necessity chain identifies one exclusive route.
